title: Electrical Engineer Salary Australia: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to calculate an electrical engineer salary Australia from hourly rates using 38-hour weeks, plus tax, super, and casual loading. Fair Work Ombudsman award rates included.
salarySummary: For an electrical worker Grade 5 under the Electrical Award, the hourly rate is $31.13, giving an annual salary of about $61,516 before tax and super, assuming 38 hours per week.

faqs.q: What is the average electrical engineer salary Australia?
faqs.a: The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week, which is about $108,352 annually. However, electrical engineers often earn more than the award rates for electrical trades. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s Electrical, Electronic and Communications Contracting Award provides minimum rates for electrical workers, not professional engineers. For a precise figure, check your award or agreement.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by hours per week (usually 38) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $30 per hour × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime or penalty rates. Use the timesheet on this site to do the calculation quickly.

faqs.q: Is casual loading included in the hourly rate?
faqs.a: No. Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate for casual employees, as per the Fair Work Ombudsman. When using a calculator, enter your base rate without casual loading, then tick the casual loading box. The 25% is added automatically.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Electrical Engineer Salary Australia

When you search for an **electrical engineer salary Australia**, you’ll find figures from recruiter surveys, the Australian Bureau of Statistics, and award rates from the Fair Work Ombudsman. This article helps you convert any hourly rate into an annual figure, taking into account the standard 38-hour week, tax, the Medicare levy, and superannuation. We rely on official sources: the Fair Work Ombudsman, the Australian Bureau of Statistics, and the Australian Taxation Office.

### The 38-Hour Week Assumption

Most full-time employees in Australia work an average of 38 ordinary hours per week under awards like the Electrical, Electronic and Communications Contracting Award 2020. The Fair Work Ombudsman states that a full-time employee is engaged to work an average of 38 ordinary hours per week. To calculate annual gross pay, use the formula:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For example, if your hourly rate is $31.13 (the Grade 5 electrical worker rate including industry and tool allowances from the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guide), then:

$31.13 × 38 × 52 = $61,516.88 per year.

This is your gross annual salary before tax and super. The fortnightly pay would be $61,516.88 ÷ 26 = $2,366.03.

### Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, most electrical workers and engineers are covered by awards that set higher minimum rates. The Electrical, Electronic and Communications Contracting Award 2020 has classification levels from Grade 1 to Grade 10. For instance, an Electrical Worker Grade 5 (with industry and tool allowances) earns $31.13 per hour, as shown in the Fair Work Ombudsman pay guide. Professional electrical engineers may be covered by the Professional Employees Award or an enterprise agreement, often paying above award rates.

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave or other entitlements. The Fair Work Ombudsman states that casual employees must be paid no less than the ordinary hourly rate plus 25%. For example, a casual Grade 5 electrical worker would receive $31.13 × 1.25 = $38.91 per hour. When using a calculator, always enter your base rate without the loading, then select the casual loading option.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional cost to the employer. The super guarantee applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For an annual salary of $61,516.88, the super contribution would be $7,382.03, bringing the total employment cost to $68,898.91.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your gross annual salary is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. Using the example of $61,516.88, the tax would be approximately $10,617 (using the 2026–27 scale) plus Medicare of $1,230, leaving a take-home pay of about $49,670. This is an estimate only; your actual tax may vary based on deductions, offsets, and the Medicare levy surcharge.

### Using the Timesheet and Pay Guides

To calculate your own figures, use [the timesheet](/) on this site. Enter your base hourly rate, select your hours per week (default 38), and tick the casual loading box if applicable. The tool will show your annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. For detailed award rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. You can also check the [reference tables](/data) for minimum wages and allowances.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the Grade 5 example, weekly pay is $1,183.02, so fortnightly is $2,366.04. After tax and Medicare, the fortnightly take-home would be roughly $1,910.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay calculated here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Summary

Whether you are an electrical engineer or an electrical tradesperson, understanding how your hourly rate translates to annual salary is essential for budgeting and comparing job offers. Use the official rates from the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Bureau of Statistics rather than recruiter surveys for the most reliable benchmarks. Remember to include super and tax in your calculations. For a quick estimate, visit [the timesheet](/) or explore [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) for more examples.
